qt: to the Commission Denis Nesci (ECR), Antonella Sberna (ECR), Carlo Fidanza (ECR), Carlo Ciccioli (ECR), Marco Squarta (ECR), Alessandro Ciriani (ECR), Lara Magoni (ECR), Giuseppe Milazzo (ECR), Francesco Ventola (ECR), Sergio Berlato (ECR), Daniele Polato (ECR), Elena Donazzan (ECR), Stefano Cavedagna (ECR), Michele Picaro (ECR), Francesco Torselli (ECR), Ruggero Razza (ECR), Pietro Fiocchi (ECR), Mariateresa Vivaldini (ECR), Alberico Gambino (ECR), Paolo Inselvini (ECR), Nicola Procaccini (ECR) Subject:

The proposal, while excluding the harmonisation of housing policies, introduces property criteria and restrictions through Article 114 TFEU. The price/income thresholds, which are based on per capita rather than household figures, do not take local markets into account and can be modified by the Commission. The measure addresses demand rather than the supply shortfall. Restricting short-term lettings does not guarantee that properties will become available on the market again. Article 5 does not distinguish between investors and small owners, violating proportionality as regards the right to property (Article 17 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights). In light of the above: 1.

On what evidence does the Commission consider that common thresholds based on the price/income ratio, without proper consideration of local markets and rental dynamics, comply with the principle of subsidiarity?
What estimates has it made regarding the impact of these restrictions on property value, investment and housing supply?

Does it not think that the crisis should be tackled by means of incentivising supply, rather than by restricting the right to property and undermining the legitimate ability to manage one’s own property freely, which in many cases has been purchased with savings accumulated over years and years of sacrifice?
